title: StreamSession shim: lightweight session/handler primitives for Python streaming chat ergonomics
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary: Build a compact, well-documented StreamSession shim in the Python SDK that provides a pragmatic, low-footprint surface for streaming chat completions and event handling. The shim aims to be a thin integration layer that lets app engineers opt into either: (1) async iterator-first consumption, (2) callback-first consumption, or (3) a hybrid mode that exposes structured event callbacks while still supporting incremental token iteration.

Goals:
- Provide a single, discoverable entrypoint (StreamSession) that wraps the network stream and emits typed events (token, delta, meta, end, error).
- Support deterministic teardown and cancellation with graceful drain of in-flight batches and optional checkpoint emission for resumable retries.
- Built-in idempotent retry hooks that can replay safe idempotent segments (prefix-resume) without leaking duplicate user-visible fragments.
- Small API surface (~3 public classes/functions) and minimal runtime overhead so it can be used in latency-sensitive code paths.

Anti-goals (out-of-scope for this ticket):
- Full-blown saga/transaction framework.
- Large stateful persistent checkpoint store (we'll expose hooks for integrations).
- Language-level backward compatibility guarantees across major versions (that will be part of a broader SDK policy).

Deliverables:
1) StreamSession class with: start(), async iterator (.tokens()), on(event, handler) callback registration, close()/abort(), and resume(token) helper.
2) Typed event names: "token", "delta", "meta", "complete", "error", "watermark".
3) Retry policy helpers: idempotent_prefix_resumer and conservative_backoff for soft/none retries.
4) Example cookbook: two small recipes (iterator-first and callback-first) plus a migration guide from existing stream APIs.
5) Unit tests (happy path, cancellation, resume, duplicate suppression) and a small e2e integration test against the test sandbox stream endpoint.

Minimal API example (developer-facing):

from redwood_sdk.streaming import StreamSession

async with StreamSession(model="redwood-chat-v1", prompt=prompt) as s:
    # callback-first consumption
    def on_token(tok):
        print(tok, end="", flush=True)
    s.on("token", on_token)

    # iterator-first consumption still possible
    async for chunk in s.tokens():
        # chunk is a small typed object: {text, role, sequence_id}
        pass

    # close() triggers graceful drain; abort() cancels immediately

Notes on semantics:
- The shim will coalesce adjacent tokens from the same sequence_id and expose a watermark event to help dedupe/commit checkpoints.
- Resume(token) expects a stable resume token generated by the StreamSession; not intended to be a durable store format (integration point for a migration task).
acceptance_criteria: StreamSession implemented and exported in redwood_sdk.streaming and covered by unit tests
Support for both iterator-first and callback-first consumption with clear examples in the cookbook
Deterministic close() behavior: drains in-flight tokens and emits complete event within configured SLO or returns error
Retry helper implemented and exercised by an integration test that demonstrates idempotent-prefix resume without visible duplication
Telemetry hooks emit token counts, stream duration, and retry counts to internal sandbox dashboard link
decisions: Expose both async iterator and callback registration to minimize migration friction for existing users.
Keep typed events small and explicit to discourage ad-hoc string parsing in consumer code.
Implement duplicate suppression at the shim level using sequence_id + watermark rather than pushing complexity onto server-side resume tokens.
Do not persist resume tokens by default; expose hooks so platform teams can wire their own durable checkpoint store.
Telemetry: emit structured metrics (counter: tokens, gauge: inflight, histogram: latency) via existing SDK telemetry facade.
notes: Trade-offs: coalescing tokens reduces callback churn but may slightly increase per-chunk latency. We prefer a configurable coalesce window (default 10ms).
Alternative considered: only iterator-first API to reduce surface area. Rejected because many customers use callback/websocket-first patterns.
Retry model: we avoid optimistic at-most-once semantics for the first pass. We'll provide conservative helpers and document pitfalls for idempotency-sensitive integrators.
Security: shim won't change data plane encryption. Any stored resume tokens should be treated as PII-equivalent by consumers.
